text:
name: move_to_savings
does: Moves money from one of your own accounts into another one, like checking to savings.
inputs: the amount, the account to take it from, and the account to put it in
people say:
- Put fifty into my savings
- I want to set money aside for my tax bill
- Shift some cash from my main account to the gold card account
- Pack away twenty a week for the trip
- Can you take a hundred out of checking and park it somewhere safe?

Many phones can read text aloud. This helps people who cannot see the screen well, or who are tired of reading. You can ask the phone to read an email, a web page or a message out loud. If the voice is too fast, you say, slower please. If a word is not correct, you can ask the phone to spell it one letter at a time. You can also ask for bigger text, which is useful when you wash the dishes and look at a recipe from far away. A person reading a letter about their salary may want the words larger too. People say, make the words bigger, or, talk to me instead of showing me. Each change is a small setting, and an assistant can switch it for you.

They want to hear more news headlines than usual.
More news please
Double the headlines today
Give me more than three stories this time
Can you read me twice as many headlines as yesterday? I am drinking my milk and I have time.
Is there any news about the young goalkeeper, and will his leg heal in time for Saturday?
Keep going, I want less talk about the weather and more local news
Half a dozen headlines, not just two
I would be very happy if you could read a few more stories, since I have a long wait and nothing else to do
Don't stop yet, what else is in the news?

Omar woke up late and felt half asleep. He reached for his phone and said, "What is on my list today?" The assistant read out three tasks: call the dentist, take out the bins, and weigh the parcel for his sister. Omar yawned. "Move the parcel to tomorrow at seven, and put soup on the shopping list." The assistant moved the parcel task to seven tomorrow morning and added soup to the shopping list. Then Omar said, "Check off the dentist, I called yesterday." The assistant marked it done. Omar looked at the north window, where frost still covered the glass. Only two tasks were left, so he made coffee first.

name: check_pantry
does: Tells you if you still have a food or item at home and about how much is left.
inputs: the name of the food or thing
people say:
- Do we have any rice left?
- Am I out of coffee again?
- Is there even a spoon of sugar in the jar?
- I feel like we are low on eggs, can you check?
- Do I have extra flour for the weekend?

They want to know the temperature outside right now.
How warm is it out there?
Temperature?
Is it pretty cold outside?
Is it above twenty-five degrees out there?
How many degrees is it right now?
Could you tell me the temperature before I take the dog out?
The soup is ready to serve, but I want to eat on the porch. Is it warm enough?
I am standing at the cupboard looking for a jacket. What is it like outside?
Please tell me how hot or cold it is outside, if it is not too much trouble.

People count days all the time. How many days until the big trip? How old will Grandma be next month? A phone can do the counting for you. You give it a date, and it tells you how many days, weeks or months are left. This is useful when you wait for a birthday, a holiday or a deadline. When plans move, people change the date and say, make it Friday instead, or, count from the first of June. If you want to hear the answer, you can ask the assistant to say it out loud. You can also ask it to count things, like how many weeks are in a school term, and it will give you a short number back.

A baby's day is made of small times: when to feed, when to nap, when to change. Many parents ask a phone or a speaker to remember them. A feeding timer rings after a number of hours, like three. A baby monitor lets you look at the baby or listen from another room. Sometimes it gives a false alarm when the baby just turns over, so parents ask it to be less sensitive. They change things with words like, remind me in two hours, make the nap alarm later, or, turn the monitor up. The goal is simple: a rested baby and a parent who does not have to remember everything.

A recipe is written for a certain number of servings. If you cook for more or fewer people, you scale it. Double means every cup and spoon doubles. Half means you cut each one in half. Cooks say, make this for six, or, I only need half of that. A voice assistant can do the sums while your hands are busy. You can ask how many spoons are in a cup, or ask for a mild version with less pepper. If the numbers feel strange, a good cook takes a breath, smiles and asks again. The goal is the same taste, just a different size.

Lena was texting from her bedroom. Her grandfather lived alone in a small flat, and she worried about his pills. She typed to the assistant on her phone: grandpa's pill box is still full and it is already night. The assistant understood that she was afraid he had missed his medicine. It set a daily reminder on his tablet, which was on loan from her school, for eight every morning. Then Lena wrote, remove the old reminder for the blue pill, he stopped taking it. The assistant removed it and said so. Last, Lena asked for a text whenever Grandpa marked a pill as taken, and the assistant said it would send one.

Person: My cat is gone.
Assistant: I am sorry to hear that. What does your cat look like?
Person: He is orange and he has a white spot on his head, like a little cap.
Assistant: Do you want me to put a lost cat notice on the neighbourhood board?
Person: Yes, it is important. Please do it now.
Assistant: When should the notice go up on the board?
Person: Tomorrow at seven, before I go to school.
Assistant: Okay. I will send it at seven tomorrow morning.
Person: Can you stretch it to the next street too?
Assistant: I can only post to your own street, but I can ask your neighbours to share it.

Grandpa Joe was hungry, but he wanted to walk to the shop before lunch. He typed on his phone in a hurry: will it rane this afternoon. The assistant understood that he was asking about rain today. It said there was a small chance of rain after three o'clock. Joe typed again: undo that, i meant tomorrow. The assistant dropped the first question and told him tomorrow would be dry and sunny. At the shop, a customer in front of him was grumbling about the wet weather. Joe smiled. He had learned that today might bring rain and tomorrow would be dry, so he bought bread and went home before three.

Person: Can you translate a note for my son's teacher?
Assistant: Of course. Which language should it be in?
Person: Spanish. Tell her he has a rare allergy to dust.
Assistant: Got it. What else should the note say?
Person: Please ask her to keep the air purifier on in the classroom. Say he needs a clean desk each morning, and that I will call her tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Here is the note in Spanish. Should I send it to the school, or only show it to you?
Person: Only show it to me. I will print it.

Your home uses electricity all day, and a meter counts how much. Many people want to use less, so they play with a few settings: they turn down the heat, switch off lights, and run the washing machine at night, when power can be cheaper. Solar panels on a roof make power from the sun. On a bright day they can cover a lot of what the house needs, and the height and angle of the roof matter. People ask an assistant, how much power did I use today, or, turn everything off in the living room, or, tell me when the sun is making the most power. Small changes add up over a month.

name: gentle_wake_alarm
does: Rings an alarm that slowly gets louder at the time you choose.
inputs: the wake-up time, and which days it should ring
people say:
- Wake me up easy at six
- I have a busy day, get me up by half past five
- I have to drive to the airport early, set something for four
- I will plug my phone in tonight, so ring me at six thirty on weekdays
- Make it softer, I don't want to scare the baby

Ruth was on her knees by the flower bed when the shed door began to stick. She grabbed her phone and typed in a hurry: find a handyamn to fix my shed door, it is important, rain comes thursday. The assistant understood that she needed a repair person before Thursday. It looked up two handymen nearby and said one could come on Wednesday morning. Ruth said yes, so the assistant booked him. Then she asked it to tell the man to paint the door too and to bring a new key for the lock. The assistant added both things to the booking and told Ruth it was done. She went back to her roses.

Priya came home after a night shift, tired but hungry for fresh bread. She put flour on the counter and said to the kitchen speaker, "I want bread ready tomorrow at seven, before I leave for work." The assistant said the dough should rise for about eight hours, so she should start tonight. Priya asked what weight of flour she needed. The assistant said five hundred grams for one loaf. She poured it out, then said, "Wake me in an hour, I am going to climb into bed." The assistant set the timer. Priya said bad bread was worse than no bread, so the assistant offered to remind her to check the dough at the right time.

Lost pets are a common worry on a street. A collar tag with a phone number is perfect for getting a pet home fast, and some tags come in a bright brand colour that is easy to spot. People also post a photo in the local group and say, help me find my dog, or, tell the street. Another thing neighbours talk about is noise. If a party is loud, they say, ask them to turn it down, or, set quiet hours. A list of local events shows when there is a street sale or a school fair, and you can ask an assistant, what is on this weekend, or, remind me about the fair.

Marco was a cook, and his hands were covered in dough. His phone buzzed on the shelf, and he did not want to touch it. He wore a grey hoodie with the sleeves pushed up. "Read my messages out loud," he said, "but not the long ones." The assistant understood that he wanted only short messages. It read two. The first asked him to pack ten lunch boxes for the school trip. The second said the delivery would come at noon. Marco asked the assistant to reply to the first one with the word okay, in a neat short line. The assistant sent it and said so. Marco nodded and went back to the dough.

A radio picks up stations from the air. You turn a dial or say a station's name to tune in. Many people listen to the news on the radio at breakfast, or even while they bathe. In the afternoon some like talk shows, and the last thing at night they like soft music. A radio can also be a nice present for a grandparent. When people want a change, they say, find the news station, or, go back to the last one, or, make it louder. Some stations are weak when you are far from the town, so you may need to turn the radio a little to hear it clearly.

name: track_package
does: Shows where a parcel is right now and when it should arrive.
inputs: the order number, or the name of the shop
people say:
- Where is my apron? I ordered it last week.
- When will my parcel come?
- Show me what is going on with the delivery
- Did the cheap shoes I ordered ship yet?
- Is my order stuck somewhere?

They want a reminder to take their medicine.
Remind me about my pills
Pill time, please
Push me to take my medicine every day at eight
Tell me softly when it is time for my tablets
Set a reminder twenty-five minutes before dinner for my heart tablet
Can you make sure I take my medicine? I keep forgetting.
My neighborhood nurse says I must not miss a dose, so please remind me
Would you mind reminding me each morning to take my pills with breakfast?

Tom drove a delivery van and was parked outside a shop at lunch. He said to his phone, "Put the company picnic on my calendar for Saturday, and read me the agenda for the call tomorrow at seven." The assistant added the picnic to Saturday. Then it read the agenda, which had three items. The first one was the repair of the loading door at the depot. Tom felt scared that his boss would ask him about the cost. He asked the assistant to remind him at six thirty tomorrow morning to join the call. The assistant set the reminder and said it was ready. Tom finished his sandwich and went back to work.

Mr. Haddad did not like new gadgets, but his doctor had asked him to walk more. He sat in front of the tv with his phone and said slowly, "Excuse me, could you please tell me how many steps I have walked today? My doctor wants to see the number, and I would like to show her that I am trying." The assistant understood that he wanted today's step count. It said he had walked four thousand two hundred steps. He then asked it to spell the word pedometer, because he wanted to write it on a card. The assistant spelled it letter by letter. Mr. Haddad smiled, put on his coat, and went out for some fresh air to add more steps.

Person: These prices mean nothing to me. I only know dollars.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which currency are the prices in?
Person: I am not sure. The shop is in Paris.
Assistant: Then they are probably euros. What is the first price?
Person: A lamp for forty, and a rug for the floor for ninety.
Assistant: Do you want both shown in dollars?
Person: Yes please. The euro is strong this year, so I want to be careful.
Assistant: I can show you the prices in dollars, but I can't tell you if the shop's price is fair. Would you like the amounts now?

Sam stood at the bus stop in the rain. His mum was at work, and he was not sure the bus would come. The sky was not clear at all, and the roof of the shelter had a leak, so drops fell on his hat. He held up his phone and said, "Next bus?" The assistant understood that he wanted to know when the next bus would come to that stop. It said the number twelve would arrive in four minutes. Sam said thanks. He moved to a dry corner of the shelter and waited. When the bus came, he got on and sat by the window.

Maya sat on her bed and texted the assistant: order the gold humidifier from the shop, the one under twenty-five dollars. i wonder if it can come by friday. The assistant understood that she wanted to buy that exact item, and it asked if it should be sent to her home. Maya said yes. The assistant placed the order, said the price was twenty-three dollars, and told her it would arrive on Thursday. Maya sent back a thumbs up. Her room had been dry all winter, and she was tired of waking up with a sore throat. She smiled and put her phone on the desk.

Luis was driving home when his phone began to glow on the dashboard. He could not look at it, so he said, "Read me my new texts." The assistant said he had twenty-five unread messages and asked if he wanted all of them. "Just the last three," said Luis. The assistant read them out. One was from his wife, asking him to buy a new handle for the kitchen cupboard. Another was from his brother, about the current score of the game. Luis said, "Reply to my wife: will do, home by six." The assistant sent the message and told him it was sent. Luis kept his eyes on the road.

Jo was at the skate park and had just landed a trick. He texted the assistant: record a video of the next one, no sound, and do not post it anywhere. The assistant understood that he wanted a silent clip that stayed private. It started the camera in digital video mode and turned the sound off. Jo said the width of the ramp was small, so he could not decide which trick to try first. The assistant said it would keep recording until he said stop. Jo shouted that he was ready and rolled forward. Afterwards the clip was saved on his phone, and it was shared with no one.

Dana was putting her son to bed with one arm full of laundry. She typed fast with her thumb: set bedtim alarm for a quarter past eight and play rain sounds. The assistant understood that she wanted a bedtime reminder at eight fifteen and some soft sounds for the room. It set the reminder and started the rain sounds at a low volume. Her son was excited about a trip on Saturday and could not sleep. Dana sat by his bed. After ten minutes the sounds had done their work, and the boy was breathing slowly. She turned off the light and carried the laundry out.

They want to start a timer for one turn in a game.
Start a timer for sixty seconds
Time this turn, please
One minute on the clock, go
Time me like a toothbrush timer, but for the game
I have to paint a picture of a cat before the sand runs out, so give me sixty seconds
Start the clock, it is Jake's turn
This game was expensive and we don't want to waste time, so please start a timer for each turn
Could you start a countdown of thirty seconds and tell us when it ends?

name: share_photo_album
does: Sends a photo album to the people you pick and keeps track of who has seen it.
inputs: the album name, and who to send it to
people say:
- Send the beach pictures to my mother
- Let Dad see the photos from the windy day
- I want the whole family to get the birthday album
- Who has looked at the pictures I sent?
- Show my sister everything from last summer

Walter was sweeping crumbs from the kitchen floor while the vent hummed over the stove. He had a stale loaf in his hand and wanted to plan the week. He spoke to the speaker slowly. "What can I cook this week? I want less meat and double the vegetables." The assistant understood that he wanted a dinner plan with less meat and twice as many vegetables. It gave five dinners: bean soup, a big salad with eggs, vegetable pasta, rice with peas, and fish with potatoes. Walter said the plan sounded good and asked it to put the shopping on his list. The assistant added beans, peas and carrots, and told him it was done.

A lawn needs a haircut every week or two in summer. You can push a mower yourself, or let a robot mower do the work. The robot whispers across the grass and goes back to its station when it is tired. A sprinkler gives the grass water, usually early in the morning, so the sun does not dry it. Clean edges make the garden look neat, and some people plant garlic near the flower beds to keep bugs away. People ask an assistant, cut the grass shorter, or, water the front lawn for ten minutes, or, do not mow when it rains. Small changes to the schedule are easy to say aloud.

Kai had moved to the city this year and did not know it well. He sat on the sofa and asked the assistant, "Show me the top videos about the subway." The assistant found a list of the most watched videos and began to play the first one, a short guide to buying tickets. Kai frowned. "Sorry, I meant the bus, not the subway." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It stopped the first video and showed the top videos about the bus instead. Kai picked one about night routes and watched it twice, so he could remember the stops.

A podcast is a show with many episodes, and an audiobook is a book that is read to you in chapters. Your phone remembers where you left off, so you can start again in the same place. People listen while they cook, walk, or wash at the sink. If you sneeze and miss a part, you can say, go back thirty seconds. If the speaker is too slow, you say, play it faster, and if you want to sleep, you say, stop in twenty minutes. Some shows are free, and some are paid, and you can ask the assistant, find the next episode, or, what chapter am I on?

Dana had two minutes before the train and grabbed her umbrella from the hook. She said to her phone, "Play my top songs, but not the slow ones." The assistant understood that she wanted fast songs from her most played list. It started a lively song and made it loud enough to hear in the hallway. Then Dana said, "Rank my songs from this month." The assistant read out the three most played ones. The automatic doors of the station opened as she ran in, and the music was still playing in her ears. She made the train with a few seconds to spare.

When you book a hotel room, you say how many nights you will stay and how many guests will come. Check-in is usually in the afternoon, and check-out is in the morning, so guests pack their bags before breakfast. If plans change, people say, add one more night, or, make it two guests instead of three, or, I want the least expensive room. Some guests also ask for a quiet room, or a vegetable meal at breakfast. Each of these is a small change to the booking. The hotel keeps a note of them and shows it to the staff when you arrive.

Grandma Pat stood in the hall holding one boot. She wanted music in every room. She typed with one finger: put the front room speaker with the kithcen one. The assistant understood that she wanted the two speakers to play together as a group. It joined the front room speaker and the kitchen speaker, then asked her which song to play. Pat named her favourite old song. She asked the assistant to tag the group as the house speakers, so that she could say that name later. The assistant did it and told her the name was saved. Pat put her boot down and listened.

name: evening_check_in
does: Sends a short message to a family member each evening to say that all is well.
inputs: who to message, and what time
people say:
- Let my daughter know I am home safe, even if it rains
- Tell my son I left the clinic and I am fine
- Every night at eight, say good night to my family for me
- I don't want them to worry, so please check in with them
- Message Anna that I took my pills and I am going to bed

The sea comes in and goes out twice a day. These are called tides. A beach feels different at high tide and low tide, and swimmers should know which one is coming. Near the shore, a channel of fast water can pull a swimmer away, so people stay near the flags. Noisy waves are often a sign of strong water. Sun cream protects your skin, and you put it on again after swimming. In winter, when it may snow near the coast, the water gets very cold. People ask an assistant, when is high tide, or, how warm is the water, or, remind me to put on more cream.

Elsie was watering her tomatoes from a red bucket when she remembered to call her son. She said to her phone, "What time is it in Lisbon?" The assistant said it was a quarter past three there. Elsie shook her head. "No, wait, I meant Madrid." The assistant understood that she had fixed the city. It said it was a quarter past four in Madrid. Her son had a temporary job there and a band practice at five. Elsie asked the assistant to remind her to call at four thirty. It set the reminder. She put the bucket down, wiped her hands and went to find a hat.

The world is split into time zones, so it is not the same time everywhere. When it is morning in one city, it can be night in another. Clocks tell you the time where you are, and your phone can show the time somewhere else too. People keep a short list of cities for family or work. Ask an assistant, what time is it in Tokyo, or, add London to my list. Someone riding a bike home may say, is it too late to call my sister in Paris? A good habit is to check before you ring, and say sorry if you wake a friend.

Person: Check leaks.
Assistant: Sure. Which room do you want me to check?
Person: The bathroom. I saw a spider near the pipe, and the floor is wet.
Assistant: Is water running right now, or did it stop?
Person: It runs a little. Can you close the main valve for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't close a valve in your house. You can turn it by hand, near the water meter.
Person: I am new here and I don't know where that is.
Assistant: Many homes keep it close to the kitchen sink or in the basement. I can also call a plumber for you.

Mrs. Lopez had been a teacher for forty years and now spent her mornings at home. A sudden idea came to her: she wanted her grocery list on paper, and she wanted the old school letter saved on the computer. She said to the printer, "Print my grocery list and scan this letter." The assistant understood that there were two jobs. It sent the list to the printer, and then asked her to put the letter on the glass. Mrs. Lopez hated paper jams, so she held her breath. Both jobs went well, and the scan was saved in her documents folder.

name: nearest_stop
does: Finds the closest bus or train stop to where you are and points you toward it.
inputs: your address, or where you are now
people say:
- Where can I catch a bus near here?
- It is cloudy and I am lost, which way is the closest stop?
- I am at the library, how far is the train?
- Point me to the nearest station
- Is there a stop on my street?

Person: I am standing at the door in a T-shirt, and the sky looks grey.
Assistant: Do you want to know the temperature, or if it will rain?
Person: Will my clean washing dry outside today?
Assistant: Which city are you in?
Person: I am new here. It is Leeds.
Assistant: There is a chance of rain this afternoon, and the air is cool. The washing may stay damp.
Person: I saw a video where they say the water boils faster with a lid. Can you tell me about that?
Assistant: I can only help with weather and your home settings in this chat. A lid does help, though, if you want to try it.

They want to know what to do for a small cut on a finger.
i cut my finger wat do i do
Help, I cut myself
What do I put on a cut?
I was slicing an apple and the knife slipped, now my finger is bleeding
I was scoring a thick loaf of bread and cut my hand, should I wrap it?
How do I stop a little cut from bleeding?
Could you tell me how to clean and cover a small cut, please?

Ben was late and shouted at the house, "Turn on the hall light!" The assistant switched on the hall light. Ben put his keys on the table and then said, "No wait, the kitchen light, not the hall." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It turned off the hall light and switched on the kitchen light. Ben looked at the room and said, "Make it a warm colour, not that cold white." The assistant changed the colour to a warm yellow. Ben grabbed his bag, said thanks, and ran out of the door with a minute to spare.

Mina came in from the garden with mud on her boots and a plan for the afternoon. She said to the pool controller, "Check the water temperature and start the pump." The assistant understood that there were two jobs. It said the water was twenty-six degrees and started the pump. Mina's husband liked to jog around the pool, so she asked if the gate lock was shut. The assistant said it was locked. She also said the cover felt too tight and was hard to pull. The assistant told her it could not change the cover, but it would remind her to loosen the straps tomorrow.
